name: Stripe
description: Financial infrastructure platform for internet commerce
evidence: Stripe Engineering Strategy: 'Sorbet, a custom static type checker for Ruby developed by Stripe written in C++, provided structure and safety to keep the core codebase maintainable as we scaled without prematurely decomposing into microservices.'

Stripe Architecture: 'Stripe separates payment processing from its Ledger system. The payment processor handles bank latencies, retries, and idempotency keys, while the Ledger serves as an immutable, auditable system of record.'
Stripe Reliability Post: 'Targeting 99.9995% uptime using asynchronous event-driven processing so the system never blocks on database writes during peak global transaction spikes.'

Stripe Data Plane Engineering: 'Moved beyond off-the-shelf Envoy proxies to build a custom high-performance distributed proxy architecture specifically designed to route mission-critical payment traffic.'

name: Supabase
description: Open source Firebase alternative built on PostgreSQL
evidence: Supabase Architecture: 'Supabase Realtime is built using Elixir and the Phoenix Framework, streaming PostgreSQL Write-Ahead Log (WAL) changes via WebSockets to handle millions of concurrent connections.'

Supabase Systems Blog: 'Supabase ETL is a high-performance PostgreSQL replication and Change Data Capture (CDC) engine written in Rust for initial data synchronization and live replication pipelines.'
Supabase AI Post: 'First-class support for pgvector enables vector similarity search directly within PostgreSQL using HNSW and IVFFlat indexing alongside standard SQL queries.'
Supabase Storage & Auth: 'Object storage with edge auth validation and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) enforcement to maintain multi-tenant data isolation.'

name: Vercel
description: Frontend cloud and developer experience platform
evidence: Vercel Engineering: 'Turbopack uses the Turbo Engine, an incremental memoization framework written in Rust that treats compilation as a reactive dependency graph where function results are cached.'
Next.js App Router Architecture: 'Maintains a unified module graph across client and server environments, enabling React Server Components (RSC) with fine-grained task caching.'
Vercel Edge Runtime: 'Demand-driven compilation compiles only modules actually requested by the development server, eliminating eager bundling overhead.'
Vercel Infrastructure: 'Zero-config preview deployments orchestrating distributed serverless functions, asset hashing, and instant atomic rollback.'

name: Anthropic
description: AI safety and research company building reliable Claude models
evidence: Anthropic API Engineering: 'Prompt Caching implements prefix KV-cache reuse with explicit cache_control breakpoints, reducing input token costs by up to 90% and slashing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT).'
Anthropic Inference Optimization: 'Combining prompt caching with speculative decoding, using a smaller draft model to predict token sequences verified by Claude 3.5 Sonnet in a single parallel pass.'
Anthropic Platform: 'Designing low-latency streaming APIs for Claude 3.5 Sonnet, tool-use evaluation harnesses, and enterprise batch processing pipelines.'
Anthropic Research: 'Constitutional AI and automated red-teaming pipelines for evaluating model harmlessness, factuality, and multi-turn tool use reliability.'

name: Datadog
description: Observability and security platform for cloud-scale applications
evidence: Datadog Systems Engineering: 'The Datadog Agent is written in Go and manages the lifecycle of sandboxed eBPF programs written in C to hook kernel syscalls with minimal CPU overhead.'
Datadog Cloud Network Monitoring: 'Replaced high-overhead Netlink polling with eBPF to accurately attribute network connections to specific PIDs and container runtimes.'
Datadog Security Research: 'Scaling real-time file monitoring with eBPF ring buffers, filtering billions of kernel events per minute before transmitting telemetry to user space.'
Datadog Data Pipeline: 'Universal Service Monitoring using eBPF protocol tracing to automatically map Kafka, gRPC, and HTTP dependencies without manual instrumentation.'
